items.headline: Greed falls five points to 83 while valuation remains at 85 after Monday's technology selloff
items.summary: The 25 August AGCI snapshot places Greed at 83/100, down 5 points daily, while Valuation remains 85/100. The regime is Mid Bull, confidence is 73/100 and the matrix remains EUPHORIA_RISK — Capital preservation / Do not chase. The S&P 500 input closed 24 August at 7,652.86 and VIX rose to 15.85.
items.whyItMatters: Psychology has cooled but valuation has not reset. AGCI treats the decline as improved optionality, not a broad buy signal, and keeps liquidity available ahead of Nvidia, PCE/GDP and Jackson Hole.
items.agciSignal: GREED COOLING / VALUATION STILL EXTREME / KEEP OPTIONALITY

items.newsletter: Review & Preview — Tech’s Long Slide — 24 Aug 2026
items.headline: Technology records a seventh consecutive down session, the longest losing streak since 2022
items.category: Technology / Equities / Market Breadth / Capital Allocation
items.summary: Barron's flagged that technology stocks fell for a seventh straight session on 24 August, the sector's longest losing streak since September 2022. The move arrives immediately before Nvidia earnings and after a period of extreme AI valuation and capex expectations.
items.whyItMatters: A multi-session drawdown can create selective entry points, but AGCI does not equate duration of a selloff with cheap valuation. The correct response is to distinguish self-funded platforms and infrastructure leaders from high-duration or externally financed AI exposure.
items.agciSignal: TECH RESET IN PROGRESS / SELECTIVITY > BETA / DO NOT FRONT-RUN NVDA

items.headline: Options imply roughly a $280 billion Nvidia market-value swing around earnings
items.summary: Reuters reports that options traders are pricing a roughly $280 billion move in Nvidia's market capitalization around its 26 August results. The report comes as investors scrutinize the sustainability and financing quality of the AI spending cycle rather than only top-line growth.
items.whyItMatters: The event is large enough to move the semiconductor complex and broad technology indices. AGCI avoids a binary pre-earnings position and instead prepares post-report scenarios around revenue, margins, Rubin demand, customer financing and capex quality.
items.agciSignal: EVENT VOLATILITY EXTREME / SIZE POSITIONS CONSERVATIVELY / REASSESS AFTER PRINT

items.headline: U.S. broadens Iran sanctions threat but initially stops short of immediate penalties on third countries; oil falls
items.summary: Reuters reports that Washington warned countries to cut business ties with Iran or risk secondary sanctions, but did not immediately impose the broad third-country penalties markets had feared. On 25 August oil fell more than 3% to a one-week low as traders judged the first step less disruptive than expected, while Iran vowed resistance.
items.whyItMatters: The realized policy was less severe than the pre-event tail case, lowering immediate oil-supply risk but leaving escalation optionality intact. AGCI reduces the urgency to add energy hedges after the move, while retaining protection against a later expansion toward Chinese banks, refiners or shipping.
items.agciSignal: SANCTIONS BELOW WORST-CASE / OIL RISK PREMIUM EASES / KEEP TAIL HEDGE

items.newsletter: U.S. equity futures / catalyst setup — 25 Aug 2026
items.headline: Technology attempts a rebound while markets wait for Nvidia and inflation data
items.summary: Reuters reports U.S. stock futures edging higher on 25 August as technology attempted to recover from Monday's decline. The market remains concentrated around Nvidia results and the next inflation and growth releases, with rate sensitivity elevated.
items.whyItMatters: A pre-event rebound does not resolve the underlying valuation and rate-risk debate. AGCI keeps a neutral tactical stance until earnings and macro data validate either a renewed risk-on regime or a deeper reset.
items.agciSignal: TACTICAL REBOUND / CATALYST RISK UNRESOLVED / WAIT FOR CONFIRMATION
